title: Initial-D inspired car racing game prototype playable in any browser. Custom vehicle and physics engine built with Claude Code on top of three.js
author: mediumbrownfox
selftext:
This is an early prototype to build out the in-game track editor and get the core drift feeling nice.

This was completely vibe coded in a few weeks a few hours a day (I'm working on other projects too).  

The game is pretty hard! especially with a keyboard but with some practice you can do some epic long drifts.  I cant wait to play this against someone else! 

That is a ghost car behind with my best track time and it also captured the drift skid marks of the rear wheels to give a new player an idea of when and where to start a drift. 

Next step is online multiplayer and also improving the visual effects, I'd like to get more foliage and trees to really get the Touge feel.  I do have a wet weather mode which needs some work, but its also pretty decent.  

I think I'll probably open this up when we get multiplayer going and see what y'all do with it.  The goal for this is for everyone can have their own home track and hang out with their friends, tune cars and also create teams to battle other teams on their home track. 

Has anyone got some good libraries for VFX?

comments.author: Secret_Slide_1357
comments.body:
Wow amazing work! Looks amazing!   
Maybe have the ghost have reduced opacity? I guess you haven't really tackled this yet.  
Either way amazing work! Congrats!

replies.author: mediumbrownfox
replies.body: Thanks!  Yeah the ghost was an issue that needs more time.  I'm still pretty new to blender and just didnt have time to learn how to edit the model so i was trying to prompt claude to reduce the opacity of the model, but the interior details of the model show through and it looks really noisy.  I need to spend more time on this or get a modeler to create a new ghost model.  Might try blender MCP this week to see if that works.

comments.author: __Maximum__
comments.body: The whole game was vibe coded? Are you a dev? Have you prompted the stack, architecture or anything else or did it decide everything on its own?

replies.author: mediumbrownfox
replies.body:
Whole game was vibe coded.  I didnt write a single line of code nor would I even be capable of writing a physics engine. 

I did try making this game a few months ago but using cannon.js and ammo.js as the vehicle physics but they just never worked and always had weird issues with the car wheels not being in the right place or pointing the wrong direction.  

Initially i just prompted claude with a PRD of the game overview, and told it to write a custom vehicle physics engine that would work for the style of game and features that I wanted.  Then it worked out the stack itself.  

I also run --dangerously-skip-permissions but i haven't found its gone off track too much.  I dont recommend unless you're pretty good at prompting though.

replies.author: __Maximum__
replies.body: It's weird that importing a physics library did not work well. I was also surprised that models can write pretty good physics engine themselves. I asked gemini to do it on aistudio. But it wasn't better than the one it imported obviously and it's weird that in your case the imported engine did not work well. Maybe try on aistudio.

replies.author: mediumbrownfox
replies.body: The custom engine works fine (for now).   I did try using Gemini 3 in Factory for some tasks but Opus 4.5 seems to do it a lot better.  Thanks for the feedback!
